The '''2016 Football League Cup final''' was a [[association football|football]] match played at [[Wembley Stadium]], [[London]], on 28 February 2016 to determine the winner of the [[2015–16 Football League Cup]], the 56th edition of the [[Football League Cup]], a competition for the 92 teams in the [[Premier League]] and [[English Football League|Football League]]. It was contested by [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], with Manchester City winning 3–1 in a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] after the match had finished 1–1 after [[Overtime (association football)|extra time]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2016/feb/28/liverpool-v-manchester-city-capital-one-cup-final-live |title=Liverpool 1 Man City 1 (Man City win 3-1 on penalties) |date=28 February 2016 |work=The Guardian |access-date=8 March 2016 }}</ref> They would have qualified for the Third Qualifying Round of the [[2016–17 UEFA Europa League]], but they ultimately qualified for the [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League]] instead by virtue of their league position.<ref>{{cite journal |url=http://kassiesa.net/uefafiles/2015-18-uefa-access-list-explanations.pdf |title=UEFA access list 2015–18 |publisher=Kassiesa |access-date=26 January 2016 |archive-date=4 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404101248/https://kassiesa.net/uefafiles/2015-18-uefa-access-list-explanations.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Background==
Liverpool were participating in a record 12th League Cup final, having previously won a record eight, most recently in [[2012 Football League Cup final|2012]] against [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]]. Their last loss was in [[2005 Football League Cup final|2005]] to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]].<ref>{{cite web|first=JJ |last=Bull |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/liverpool/12122276/Liverpool-Stoke-City-Capital-One-League-Cup-semi-final-second-leg-TV-live.html |title=Liverpool vs Stoke City, League Cup semi-final: Mignolet sends Liverpool to Wembley with penalty shootout saves |work=Daily Telegraph |access-date=26 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Hunter|first=Andy|title=Joe Allen fires Liverpool to Wembley in shootout win over Stoke City|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/jan/26/liverpool-stoke-city-capital-one-cup-match-report|access-date=7 February 2016|work=The Guardian}}</ref>

Manchester City made their fifth appearance in the final, having won three previous times, the last of which as recently as [[2014 Football League Cup final|2014]] against [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26311649 |title=Manchester City 3–1 Sunderland |work=BBC Sport |date=2 March 2014 |access-date=1 February 2016 }}</ref>

Liverpool, as a [[Premier League]] team involved in the [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League]], started the competition in the third round. In this they were drawn against [[Football League Two]] team [[Carlisle United F.C.|Carlisle United]], at their home ground, [[Anfield]]. After [[Overtime (association football)|extra time]] the score was 1–1 but Liverpool advanced after a 3–2 [[penalty shoot out]] win.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34265500|title=Liverpool 1–1 Carlisle United (3–2 pens)|work=BBC Sport|access-date=26 January 2016}}</ref> In the fourth round they were drawn at home again, this time against fellow Premier League team [[A.F.C. Bournemouth|AFC Bournemouth]]; they won the game 1–0 after [[Nathaniel Clyne]]'s debut goal for Liverpool.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34589602|title=Liverpool 1–0 Bournemouth|work=BBC Sport|access-date=26 January 2016}}</ref>

In the quarter finals, they were drawn away to fellow Premier League team [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]]. At [[St. Mary's Stadium]], Liverpool won 6–1 with a [[hat-trick]] from [[Divock Origi]], two goals from [[Daniel Sturridge]] and one from [[Jordon Ibe]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34918281|title=Southampton 1–6 Liverpool|work=BBC Sport|access-date=26 January 2016}}</ref> In the two-legged semi-final, Liverpool were drawn against [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]]. At the [[Britannia Stadium]], Liverpool won the first leg 1–0 due to a goal from Ibe.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35155369|title=Stoke City 0–1 Liverpool|work=BBC Sport|access-date=26 January 2016}}</ref> However, they lost the second leg 1–0 at Anfield, their first home loss in a League Cup semi-final,<ref name=stoke /> necessitating a penalty shoot out which Liverpool won 6–5; goalkeeper [[Simon Mignolet]] saved from [[Peter Crouch]] and [[Marc Muniesa]] with [[Joe Allen]] scoring the winner.<ref name=stoke>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35349469|title=Liverpool 0–1 Stoke City (agg 1–1, pens 6–5)|work=BBC Sport|access-date=26 January 2016}}</ref>

Manchester City, as a Premier League team involved in the [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League]], started in the third round, in which they were drawn away against [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]]. At the [[Stadium of Light]], Manchester City won 4–1 with goals from [[Sergio Agüero]], [[Kevin De Bruyne]], [[Raheem Sterling]] and an own goal from [[Vito Mannone]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34253381 |title=Sunderland 1–4 Manchester City |work=BBC Sport |date=22 September 2015 |access-date=27 January 2016}}</ref> In the next round they were drawn at home against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]]. At the [[City of Manchester Stadium]], Manchester City won 5–1 with goals from [[Wilfried Bony]], De Bruyne, [[Kelechi Iheanacho]], [[Yaya Touré]] and [[Manu García (footballer, born 1998)|Manu García]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34589630 |title=Manchester City 5–1 Crystal Palace |work=BBC Sport |date=28 October 2015 |access-date=27 January 2016}}</ref>

In the quarter-finals, they were drawn against [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] at home, where they won 4–1 with goals from Bony, Iheanacho and two from De Bruyne.<ref>{{cite news|last=Jurejko |first=Jonathan |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34907256 |title=Manchester City 4–1 Hull City |work=BBC Sport |date=1 December 2015 |access-date=27 January 2016}}</ref> In the semi-finals, they were drawn against [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] where despite losing 2–1 at [[Goodison Park]],<ref>{{cite news|last=McNulty |first=Phil |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35155377 |title=Everton 2–1 Manchester City |work=BBC Sport |date=6 January 2016 |access-date=27 January 2016}}</ref> Manchester City won 3–1 at the City of Manchester Stadium, which included a controversial goal as Raheem Sterling failed to keep the ball from crossing the dead ball line, but the officials missed it and allowed the goal to stand thus reaching the final 4–3 on aggregate and also preventing a [[Merseyside derby]] final.<ref>{{cite news|last=McNulty |first=Phil |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35358806 |title=Manchester City 3–1 Everton (agg 4–3) |work=BBC Sport |date=1 January 1970 |access-date=27 January 2016}}</ref>

==Match==
===Summary===
In the 49th minute [[Fernandinho (footballer, born May 1985)|Fernandinho]] opened the scoring for Man City with a low shot from a tight angle on the right of the box that went into the far corner under Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet. In the 60th minute Raheem Sterling had a chance to make it 2-0 but he passed the ball wide of the near post from six yards out. In the 83rd minute, Daniel Sturridge drilled the ball in from the right beyond the far post, the ball came to [[Adam Lallana]] whose shot hit the face of the near post with the ball coming back to [[Philippe Coutinho]], who scored with a low right foot shot from 12 yards out.<ref>{{cite web |title=Liverpool vs Manchester City, League Cup final - live: City win the cup as hero Caballero makes three penalty saves |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/liverpool/12176573/Liverpool-vs-Manchester-City-League-Cup-final-2016-TV-channel-live.html |work=Daily Telegraph |date=28 February 2016 |access-date=4 August 2016 }}</ref> There were no more goals in the 90 minutes or in the 30 minutes of extra-time with the match going to a penalty shoot-out. [[Emre Can]] scored the first penalty of the shoot-out for Liverpool before Fernandinho missed the first spot-kick for Man City, hitting the post. [[Lucas Leiva]] then missed the next kick for Liverpool, with [[Willy Caballero]] diving to his left to save. [[Jesús Navas]] then scored with his kick before Philippe Coutinho missed with the next kick for Liverpool, Caballero saving again to his left. Sergio Agüero then scored before Caballero dived to his right to save from Adam Lallana. Yaya Touré scored with a low shot to the left to win the game for Man City 3-1 on penalties.<ref>{{cite web |title=Liverpool v Manchester City: Capital One Cup final – as it happened |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2016/feb/28/liverpool-v-manchester-city-capital-one-cup-final-live |work=The Guardian |date=28 February 2016 |access-date=4 August 2016 }}</ref>

== Post-match ==
In winning, Manchester City qualified for the Third Qualifying Round of the [[2016–17 UEFA Europa League]]; however, they subsequently qualified for the [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League]] via their league position. The vacant UEFA Europa League berth was instead allocated to the club ranked highest in the [[2015–16 Premier League]] that had not already qualified for Europe, which was seventh-placed [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]].
